name: NVIDIA Corporation
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: NVIDIA is this ecosystem's demand engine and architecture-setter — its rack-power roadmap (~120–150 kW GB300 racks today → ~600 kW Kyber racks with 800VDC in 2027 → 1 MW-class beyond) dictates what every power and storage supplier in the file must build, and its published 800VDC partner list is the de facto qualification slate for the next generation of data-center power. BACKGROUND: Founded 1993 by Jensen Huang; the dominant supplier of AI data-center compute (~80–85% of AI-accelerator revenue per IDC-cited estimates, down from ~92% in 2023). Fiscal years end late January: FY2026 (ended 2026-01-25) revenue was $215.9B (+65%), with the data-center segment at $193.7B. Q1 FY2027 revenue $81.6B (+85% YoY); Q2 FY2027 guided to $91B.
ecosystemRole: We assess NVIDIA as the ecosystem's gravitational center: it does not sell power or storage, but its architecture decisions create the market for both. Basis: the company itself prescribes a two-tier energy-storage hierarchy for AI factories — supercapacitors at the rack for millisecond GPU transients, and facility-level BESS at the utility interconnection for second-to-minute smoothing — and productized rack-level power smoothing in GB300 NVL72 (up to 30% peak-grid-demand reduction). Its 800VDC ecosystem list names the power vendors (Delta, LITEON, Megmeet, Flex among components; Vertiv, Eaton, Schneider, Siemens, ABB, GE Vernova, Hitachi Energy at the grid tier) who will carry the 2027 transition.

productsAndServices.name: Rack-Scale AI Compute Platforms (Blackwell → Rubin → Feynman)
productsAndServices.description: Full-rack AI systems: GB200/GB300 NVL72 (72 Blackwell-class GPUs + 36 Grace CPUs, 130 TB/s NVLink domain, liquid-cooled), Vera Rubin NVL72/NVL144 (production 2H 2026; 100% liquid-cooled MGX racks, ~3.6 EFLOPS FP4 per NVL144 per keynote figures), Rubin Ultra NVL576 in Kyber racks (2H 2027, ~600 kW/rack, 15 EFLOPS FP4), and the announced Feynman generation (Kyber NVL1152, co-packaged optics, 1 MW-class racks). GTC 2026 added the Groq 3 LPU/LPX inference rack to the platform line-up.
highlights: Rack power trajectory is the ecosystem's forcing function: >200 kW today → ~600 kW (Kyber, 2H 2027) → '1 MW IT racks and beyond' (company-stated architecture target)
GB300 NVL72 productized power smoothing: ~65 J/GPU energy storage in power shelves, ramp control, and 'GPU burn' — cutting peak grid demand up to 30% (NVIDIA-published)
Cloud GPUs 'sold out' per Huang (Q3 FY2026); supply commitments jumped from $50.3B to $95.2B in one quarter (Q4 FY2026 filing)
GB300 platform estimated at 70–80% of 2026 AI rack shipments (TrendForce), with Vera Rubin ramping 2H 2026
productsAndServices.positioning: Holds ~80–85% of data-center AI-accelerator revenue (IDC-cited estimates); AMD Instinct ~5–7%; hyperscaler custom silicon (TPU/Trainium/Maia/MTIA) ~10–20% of revenue and growing faster, concentrated in inference. Four direct customers were 61% of Q3 FY2026 revenue per the 10-Q — concentration is structural.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: ODM/CSP intermediaries (direct customers) serving hyperscalers, NVIDIA Cloud Partners, sovereign AI programs, and enterprises
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Hyperscalers, neoclouds, frontier labs, sovereign AI, enterprise AI factories
productsAndServices.roadmap: Vera Rubin production 2H 2026; Rubin Ultra NVL576/Kyber + full 800VDC in 2H 2027; Feynman generation announced at GTC 2026

productsAndServices.name: 800VDC Power Architecture Initiative
productsAndServices.category: Ecosystem architecture · directly shapes this app's supplier coverage
productsAndServices.description: NVIDIA's facility-power redesign for 1 MW-class racks: grid 13.8 kV AC → 800 VDC distribution → single-stage conversion to 12 VDC at the compute node, replacing 415/480 VAC three-phase plus in-rack 54V conversion. Published claims: ~157% more power through the same copper vs 415 VAC, up to 45% copper reduction (a 1 MW rack carries up to 200 kg of busbar on legacy architecture), up to 5% end-to-end efficiency gain, −30% TCO. Full-scale production coincides with Kyber racks in 2027.
highlights: Named partner slate (May + Oct 2025 lists): power components — Delta, LITEON, Flex, Bizlink, Lead Wealth, **Megmeet**; DC power systems — ABB, Eaton, GE Vernova, Heron Power, Hitachi Energy, Mitsubishi Electric, Schneider, Siemens, Vertiv; silicon — Infineon, TI, Navitas, onsemi, ST and others
NVIDIA prescribes storage in the architecture itself: supercapacitors rack-side for millisecond transients, facility-level BESS at the interconnection for second-to-minute smoothing
Vertiv 800VDC MGX portfolio launching 2H 2026; Eaton reference architecture released Oct 2025; Foxconn's 40 MW Kaohsiung-1 cited as first 800VDC-ready facility

BBU/supercapacitor attach economics: AI-server BBU market ~$2.8B in 2026 → ~$7.1B by 2033 (analyst est.); each GB300 cabinet ~5 BBU modules + >300 supercapacitors, with supercap supply a genuine bottleneck (trade-press analysis)
productsAndServices.positioning: The de facto standards body for AI-factory power — OCP-aligned, whitepaper-published. Delta holds an estimated ~70% of Blackwell-platform AI-server PSUs (KGI), LITEON #2; Megmeet's inclusion in both partner lists is the mainland-China exception.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Open ecosystem: reference architectures + whitepaper; partners commercialize the hardware
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Data-center power vendors, grid-equipment OEMs, hyperscale facility designers
productsAndServices.roadmap: Full-scale 800VDC production with Kyber in 2027; industry 1 MW-rack adoption projected from ~2027

productsAndServices.name: Networking, Software & Other Platforms
productsAndServices.description: NVLink scale-up (130 TB/s per 72-GPU domain; NVLink-6 with Rubin), Spectrum-X/Spectrum-6 Ethernet, Quantum InfiniBand, ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, BlueField-4 DPUs — networking revenue reached $11.0B in Q4 FY2026 alone. Software: CUDA, NIM microservices, Nemotron open-model coalition, Omniverse. Automotive/physical AI: robotaxi platforms with BYD, Hyundai, Nissan, Geely; robotics partnerships (ABB, KUKA, Universal Robots).
highlights: Networking is the quiet second franchise — $11.0B in Q4 FY2026 (~16% of the quarter)
CUDA remains the moat argument analysts cite against custom-silicon substitution
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Same ODM/CSP channel plus direct enterprise software licensing

recentDevelopments.headline: Q2 FY2027: revenue $96.2B (+106% YoY, +18% QoQ) against a $91B guide; data center $89.0B (+117%); GAAP EPS $2.46 above non-GAAP $2.22; Q3 guided to $108.0B ±2% at 74.0% gross margin
recentDevelopments.read: We assess the guide-beat cadence is intact but the earnings mix is shifting: gross margin is guided down 100bp while $7.771B of gains on NVIDIA's own equity stakes lift GAAP above non-GAAP for a second quarter. The operating business and the investment portfolio are now both material to reported earnings, and only one of them is what the multiple is being paid for.

recentDevelopments.headline: AWS to deploy 2 million additional NVIDIA GPUs across its global infrastructure in 2027-2028 — on top of the 1 million announced at GTC 2026 — spanning Blackwell Ultra, Rubin and Rubin Ultra, Vera CPU, NVLink Fusion and Spectrum networking, plus 100,000 GPUs for federal workloads
recentDevelopments.read: The largest single named hyperscaler commitment in the file by unit count, and it lands on the same day as the Q2 print. No power figure and no dollar figure are stated, so it sizes the demand signal without sizing the buildout — the gigawatt translation is the reader's to make, not the release's.

recentDevelopments.headline: Memorandums of understanding with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to establish AI compute financing platforms aiming to mobilize over $500B of third-party capital
recentDevelopments.read: We assess this externalizes the financing of NVIDIA's own demand. The instruments are memorandums of understanding rather than committed capital — the release states MOUs were 'signed with six of the world's premier financial institutions' to establish the platforms, publishes no per-firm allocation, and frames the >$500B as third-party capital the platforms aim to mobilize over time rather than an NVIDIA commitment. Read against the circular-financing critique this dossier rates the most serious structural risk, it is the largest structural answer NVIDIA has offered: it moves demand financing toward independent underwriters instead of NVIDIA's own balance sheet.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q1 FY2027: revenue $81.6B (+85% YoY) vs $78.8B consensus; Q2 guided to $91B; dividend raised 25x, +$80B buyback
recentDevelopments.read: The beat-and-raise continued yet the stock slid on the print — we assess the expectations bar, not demand, is now the binding constraint on the equity story.

recentDevelopments.read: Roadmap cadence is itself the moat — each generation resets the power/cooling bar before rivals catch the last one. The ~$1T figure is a keynote statement, not a filing.

recentDevelopments.headline: 800VDC architecture unveiled at Computex with initial partner list (Delta, LITEON, Megmeet, Eaton, Schneider, Vertiv, Infineon, TI among named)
recentDevelopments.read: The founding document of the 2027 power transition this app's supplier dossiers orbit around.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess NVIDIA has converted its compute roadmap into control of the data-center power agenda: by publishing the 800VDC architecture, naming the qualified vendor slate, and prescribing storage placement (rack supercaps + interconnection BESS), it sets the requirements every power/BESS supplier in this app must meet for the 2027 Kyber generation. Basis: NVIDIA's own technical blogs and whitepaper.

(High confidence) We assess demand is now denominated in gigawatts: OpenAI (10 GW LOI), Anthropic (up to 1 GW initial), and >1.7 GW already deployed across NVIDIA Cloud Partners. Third-party projections of ~233 GW of cumulative new AI data-center power demand 2025–2030 rest heavily on NVIDIA's shipment cadence — the single most important demand variable for this ecosystem.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the circular-financing critique is the most serious structural risk: up to $100B invested in OpenAI as it buys NVIDIA systems, reported discussions of guaranteeing up to $250B of OpenAI lease payments, and four direct customers at 61% of revenue. Bernstein and Bloomberg Intelligence analysts flag it; Burry's depreciation-understatement thesis (~$176B, 2026–2028) is the bear case NVIDIA felt compelled to rebut directly. The August 2026 compute-financing platforms — memorandums with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR aiming to mobilize over $500B of third-party capital — are the largest structural answer offered so far, moving demand financing toward independent underwriters rather than NVIDIA's balance sheet. We do not yet score it as mitigating: the instruments are memorandums, no per-firm allocation is published, and no platform has been shown funding a transaction. As of Q2 FY2027 the critique is legible in the income statement itself: $7.771B of net gains from equity securities, excluded from non-GAAP, put GAAP EPS above non-GAAP for a second consecutive quarter. Stakes taken in customers and cloud partners now move reported earnings directly, and a reversal would cut GAAP EPS below non-GAAP as mechanically as the gains lifted it.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the GB300 power-smoothing feature set (rack energy storage, ramp control, up to 30% peak-demand reduction) partially internalizes what would otherwise be BESS-supplier revenue — but simultaneously legitimizes storage-at-the-rack, expanding the BBU/supercapacitor market (~$2.8B → ~$7.1B by 2033 per analyst estimates) faster than it cannibalizes it.

(High confidence) China is now regulatory downside only: guidance assumes zero China data-center compute revenue after the H20 whipsaw ($4.5B charge, then a 15%-of-revenue export deal, then Beijing's effective blacklisting), and the SAMR Mellanox probe carries a potential ~$2.9B fine. Basis: filings, Commerce testimony, SAMR announcements.

relationships.note: 10 GW letter of intent; NVIDIA to invest up to $100B as capacity deploys — the anchor of the circular-financing critique.
relationships.context: September 2025: OpenAI signed a letter of intent for at least 10 GW of NVIDIA systems, with NVIDIA intending to invest up to $100B progressively as each gigawatt deploys (first GW on Vera Rubin in 2H 2026). The defining GW-scale demand signal — and the anchor of the circular-financing critique the dossier rates the most serious structural risk (Bernstein: will 'clearly fuel circular concerns'), alongside reported discussions of guaranteeing up to $250B of OpenAI lease payments.

relationships.note: Anthropic-Microsoft-NVIDIA partnership: up to 1 GW of Grace Blackwell/Vera Rubin capacity, NVIDIA investing up to $10B.
relationships.context: November 2025: the three-way partnership commits Anthropic initially to up to 1 GW of Grace Blackwell/Vera Rubin capacity on Azure with NVIDIA investing up to $10B — the dossier's marker that demand now arrives denominated in gigawatts, and that compute procurement has become power procurement. Microsoft is simultaneously one of the four direct customers concentrating 61% of NVIDIA revenue.

relationships.note: Grid-tier member of the 800VDC ecosystem (added at OCP 2025).
relationships.context: ABB joined NVIDIA's 800VDC ecosystem at the October 2025 OCP Summit alongside GE Vernova, Hitachi Energy, Siemens and Heron Power — the grid-equipment tier joining the partner list moved 800VDC from server-vendor concern to utility-interconnection concern, where BESS lives.

relationships.note: Grid-tier 800VDC ecosystem member with three joint AI-factory reference designs.
relationships.context: GE Vernova joined the 800VDC ecosystem at OCP 2025 and co-published AI Factory 800 VDC reference designs (grid-connected, islanded, bridging) with Omniverse DSX digital twins — the deepest grid-tier collaboration in the partner list.

relationships.note: Grid-tier 800VDC member with a co-designed grid-to-rack architecture.
relationships.context: Hitachi Energy joined the 800VDC ecosystem (OCP 2025) with a co-designed grid-to-rack power conversion architecture (company-claimed 15x power-supply increase) plus Omniverse digital-twin and DSX blueprint work announced at CERAWeek 2026.

relationships.note: Founding 800VDC partner on the power/cooling side.
relationships.context: Vertiv was on the initial 800VDC partner list at Computex (May 2025) — the founding document of the 2027 power transition — carrying the white-space power and cooling tier of the architecture into hyperscale deployments.

relationships.note: Founding 800VDC partner at the power-infrastructure tier.
relationships.context: Eaton appeared on NVIDIA's initial 800VDC partner list (Computex, May 2025) with Delta, LITEON, Megmeet, Schneider, Vertiv, Infineon and TI — the power-infrastructure names NVIDIA designated to carry the 2027 rack transition.

relationships.note: Dominant AI-server power supplier (~70% of Blackwell-platform PSUs per KGI) and founding 800VDC partner.
relationships.context: Delta holds an estimated ~70% of Blackwell-platform AI-server PSUs (KGI) and anchors the component tier of the 800VDC ecosystem from the founding Computex list — the incumbent every other power-shelf vendor is measured against.

relationships.note: #2 Blackwell-platform PSU source and founding 800VDC component-tier partner.
relationships.context: LITEON is the estimated #2 supplier of Blackwell-platform AI-server power (KGI) and a founding member of the 800VDC component tier, shipping 110 kW power shelves for Vera Rubin NVL72 and GB300-class BBU collaborations.

relationships.note: The mainland-China exception on both 800VDC partner lists; named for GB200 NVL72 power.
relationships.context: Megmeet's inclusion in both NVIDIA 800VDC partner lists is the mainland-China exception — the only mainland power vendor NVIDIA has named for GB200 NVL72 power, co-developing the 800V sidecar for the Kyber rack platform.

relationships.note: NVIDIA names Infineon among the silicon providers for its 800 VDC data-centre architecture on its own developer blog.
relationships.context:
NVIDIA's published 800 VDC ecosystem sorts partners into three tiers, and Infineon sits in the first: silicon providers, alongside Analog Devices, AOS, Efficient Power Conversion, Innoscience, Monolithic Power Systems, Navitas, onsemi, Power Integrations, Renesas, Richtek, ROHM, STMicroelectronics and Texas Instruments — fourteen names, so this is an ecosystem rather than a sole source.

The relationship went beyond listing. Infineon published a CoolSiC JFET hot-swap solution in October 2025 that lets an operator exchange a server board in an 800 VDC rack while the rest of the rack keeps running, and joined NVIDIA's MGX AI Factory ecosystem in May 2026 committing to the full 800 V to 50 V, 12 V and 6 V conversion flow with GaN bus converters near 1 MHz.

NVIDIA ties full-scale production of the architecture to its Kyber rack-scale systems in 2027. Neither party has published a revenue figure, a volume commitment or an exclusivity term.

relationships.note: NVIDIA names Flex Power among the power system components vendors for its 800 VDC architecture, and Flex has shipped power shelves built to NVIDIA platform requirements.
relationships.context:
Flex sits in the second of NVIDIA's three published tiers — power system components — with Bizlink, Delta, Lead Wealth, LITEON and Megmeet. That tier consumes the silicon the first tier supplies and feeds the facility-power systems of the third.

Flex has shipped against it: a 33 kW power shelf for the GB300 NVL72 platform at 97.5% peak half-load efficiency in August 2025, then a 110 kW shelf and an 800 VDC Power Rack for the Vera Rubin platform in March 2026, plus reference designs for NVIDIA's Omniverse DSX blueprint. Flex states it plans full-scale production of 800 VDC power components to coincide with NVIDIA Kyber rack-scale systems.

One observation belongs with it: Flex is not named in NVIDIA's May 2026 DSX partner release, nor in independent coverage of NVIDIA's GTC 2026 800 VDC ecosystem. From 2026 the announcements are largely Flex's own.

relationships.note: Collaboration with Oklo and Los Alamos National Laboratory on AI-enabled modelling, digital twins and fuel validation for plutonium-bearing fuels.
relationships.context:
Announced 23 April 2026. The direction is unusual for this corpus: compute applied to the reactor rather than the reactor applied to compute. The work supports fuel qualification for the surplus-plutonium pathway Oklo entered advanced DOE negotiations on a month later.

A parallel strand runs through Idaho National Laboratory's 'Prometheus' AI platform, integrated under a strategic partnership announced 12 May 2026 in support of Pluto, Oklo's plutonium-fuelled reactor system.

relationships.note: Thermal-management reference designs for gigawatt-scale AI factories, engineered for the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint.
relationships.context:
Announced 28 October 2025 as the first comprehensive thermal-management system reference design at gigawatt scale, supporting GB300 NVL72 and next-generation Vera Rubin systems with OpenUSD-based SimReady assets.

Optimised 16 March 2026 with a stated 10% improvement in overall thermal performance that frees 22 MW of cooling capacity for IT power, delivered as a 250 MW duplex system and a 1 GW magnetic-bearing air-cooled architecture. LiquidStack, a Trane company since March 2026, subsequently launched a GigaModular CDU built to Vera Rubin specifications and scaling to 14 MW.

relationships.note: One of six financial institutions with which NVIDIA signed memorandums of understanding to establish AI compute financing platforms (10 August 2026).
relationships.context: Announced alongside Apollo, BlackRock, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR — Blackstone and BlackRock are both named and are different firms. No per-firm allocation is published and the instrument is a memorandum, so the >$500B figure describes the programme and not Blackstone's share of it; Blackstone is not singled out with any commitment separate from the six-firm group. This is the reciprocal of the edge Blackstone's dossier already carried.
relationships.scale: one of six firms in a programme targeting >$500B of third-party capital

relationships.note: NVIDIA is a founding partner and investor in the Brookfield AI Infrastructure Fund, and named Brookfield among the six capital partners in the August 2026 financing programme.
relationships.context: Two distinct arrangements, and the figures attached to them are routinely conflated. On 19 November 2025 Brookfield launched BAIIF with a $10B equity target and $5B already committed, naming Brookfield, NVIDIA and the Kuwait Investment Authority as founding partners; the fund plus co-investment and financing is framed as acquiring up to $100B of AI infrastructure assets, and Brookfield simultaneously launched Radiant as a new NVIDIA Cloud Partner. On 10 August 2026 NVIDIA separately named Brookfield in the six-firm compute-financing programme. The $10B fund, the $100B asset programme and the >$500B six-firm figure are three different things. Reciprocal of the edge Brookfield's dossier already carried.
relationships.scale: founding partner of a $10B-target fund ($5B committed); one of six firms in the >$500B programme

relationships.note: Neocloud running NVIDIA HGX H200 clusters and contributing GPUs to the DGX Cloud Lepton marketplace. Reciprocal of the supplier edge Fluidstack's dossier already carried.
relationships.context: NVIDIA's DGX Cloud Lepton release (11 June 2025) lists Fluidstack among the providers contributing Blackwell and other NVIDIA-architecture GPUs to the marketplace, and Fluidstack deployed HGX H200 clusters with Quantum-2 InfiniBand in Iceland from March 2025. Recorded on this side because Macquarie's dossier records lending against Fluidstack's NVIDIA GPUs as collateral — the accelerators are the security in that financing — which is only legible with the NVIDIA-side edge present. NVIDIA's share of Fluidstack's 2026 fleet is not disclosed; at the US Anthropic sites the accelerators are reported to be Google TPUs.
relationships.via: HGX H200, Quantum-2 InfiniBand; DGX Cloud Lepton marketplace
relationships.scale: HGX H200 clusters (Iceland); DGX Cloud Lepton contributor
18,000 GB300 first phase; up to 600,000 GPUs over three years
relationships.via: GB300 Grace Blackwell with NVIDIA InfiniBand
relationships.note: HUMAIN, Saudi Arabia's PIF-owned AI company, bought 18,000 GB300 for its first phase and plans up to 600,000 NVIDIA GPUs over three years in Saudi Arabia and the United States.
relationships.context: NVIDIA's May 2025 release set up to 500 MW and 'several hundred thousand' GPUs over five years; HUMAIN expanded the plan in November 2025. The US approved HUMAIN for up to 35,000 GB300-equivalent chips on 19 Nov 2025, conditioned on security and reporting requirements.

relationships.note: NVIDIA supplies the Grace Blackwell GB300 systems for Stargate UAE, the 1 GW cluster G42 is building for OpenAI and Oracle, and has certified G42's Khazna data-hall designs for Blackwell.
relationships.context: NVIDIA's Q1 FY2026 results release lists Stargate UAE 'alongside strategic partners G42, OpenAI, Oracle, SoftBank Group and Cisco'. Since 10 Jul 2026 G42 and Core42 are approved licence-free recipients of advanced computing items under the BIS rule that moved the UAE to Country Group A:5. That approval expires on 6 Apr 2027 unless they become US companies.

relationships.note: NVIDIA is a Firmus shareholder, from the A$330M round of September 2025, and at Batam its partner in NVIDIA's revenue-sharing and credit-support model for neoclouds.
relationships.context: Firmus's September 2025 release: 'NVIDIA joining as an investor'; NVIDIA followed on in the US$505M and US$2B rounds of 2026. NVIDIA's own July 2026 blog names 'Sharon AI and Firmus … among the first companies to work with NVIDIA on this new business model', for a DSX AI factory campus in Batam, Indonesia. Firmus is also an NVIDIA GPU customer.

relationships.note: KKR is one of six financiers in NVIDIA's August 2026 compute-financing memoranda, and NVIDIA is a founding investor in KKR's Helix Digital Infrastructure.
relationships.context: On 10 August 2026 NVIDIA signed memoranda of understanding with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to establish compute-financing platforms aiming to mobilise over USD 500bn, 'subject to execution of the final agreements' and with no per-firm allocation. KKR's co-CEOs' statement on the partnership calls NVIDIA 'a founding investor in Helix Digital Infrastructure', which KKR's June 2026 launch release names as a cornerstone strategic partner.

relationships.note: NVIDIA advised the BlackRock-chaired AI Infrastructure Partnership from its 2024 launch and joined it in March 2025; BlackRock is one of six financiers in NVIDIA's August 2026 compute-financing memoranda.
relationships.context: BlackRock, GIP, Microsoft and MGX launched the partnership in September 2024 with NVIDIA supporting and advising; NVIDIA and xAI joined the renamed AI Infrastructure Partnership on 19 March 2025, and BlackRock's October 2025 Aligned announcement lists NVIDIA among its founders. AIP's first investment is Aligned Data Centers. In the August 2026 memoranda, Larry Fink said the deal 'deepens our relationship with NVIDIA, including through the AI Infrastructure Partnership'.

policyExposure.exposure: NVIDIA's guidance assumes zero China data-center compute revenue after the H20 whipsaw: a $4.5B export-restriction charge absorbed in Q1 FY2026 with ~$8B of guided China revenue loss, then a 15%-of-revenue export deal, then Beijing's effective blacklisting — the dossier assesses China as regulatory downside only.

China's SAMR ruled preliminarily in September 2025 that NVIDIA violated conditions of the 2020 Mellanox approval, with the investigation continuing and a potential fine of ~$2.9B — paired with the export controls, China is now regulatory downside only for NVIDIA.

periods.commentary: Reported 2026-08-26. The $91B guide set at Q1 was beaten by roughly $5.2B and the Q3 guide steps up again to $108.0B, while guided gross margin steps down 100bp to 74.0%. GAAP earnings are now materially flattered by mark-ups on NVIDIA's own equity stakes: $7.771B of net gains from equity securities in the quarter, excluded from non-GAAP, which is why GAAP EPS ($2.46) sits above non-GAAP ($2.22) — the same inversion as Q1, at roughly double the size.

metrics.result: GAAP $2.39 incl. equity gains; dividend raised 25x, +$80B buyback

periods.commentary: Q2 FY2027 guided to $91B, well above street — beaten at $96.2B when reported 2026-08-26.
Guidance assumes zero China data-center compute revenue. The one blemish of the year: Q2 FY2026 data-center revenue ($41.1B) slightly missed the $41.3B consensus — the cycle's first such miss.

metrics.result: Blackwell contributed $11.0B in Q4, above guide

periods.commentary: FY2026 Q1 absorbed a $4.5B H20 export-restriction charge with ~$8B of guided China revenue loss — later structurally excluded from guidance.

financials.commentary: Customer concentration per 10-Q filings: Q3 FY2026 had four direct customers >10% each (22/15/13/11% = 61% combined); direct customers are ODM/CSP intermediaries with ultimate demand attributed to Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, Google. Supply: TSMC CoWoS sold out through 2026 (NVIDIA reportedly >50% of it); all three HBM vendors' 2026 output sold out under non-cancellable contracts. Equity stakes now move reported earnings: net gains from equity securities were $7.771B in Q2 FY2027 and are excluded from non-GAAP, putting GAAP EPS above non-GAAP in both Q1 and Q2 FY2027.
